placements.why: The memo sets a standing organizational rule over how Meridian artifacts reach staging and production, with a named owner. Nothing in the supplied structure holds a category for release governance. The reference's Process tier (ChangeManagement: safe, auditable changes; QualityReviewGates: sign-offs) is the closest location, so the category is located there and named in the memo's own terms.
placements.title: Release gating moves from trusting artifacts to verifying them before they ship
placements.frame: What must be verified about an artifact before it is allowed to reach an environment, and which deploy paths does that verification now cover?

placements.title: Unsigned artifacts stop being able to reach environments
placements.frame: What does the gate verify before a deploy ships, and which unsigned path does it close for staging and production?
placements.why: Quinton's statement and the memo's decision record both state a standing requirement that every Meridian deploy carry a signed release manifest before it ships, applying to staging and production. This is a durable subject future envelopes will keep feeding (deploy integrity and what must hold before release), not a one-time event. The incident that prompted it is cited as support and is not given its own leaf.
